feedback.author: johnnynunez
feedback.body:
### Note for reviewers testing on consumer Blackwell (sm120)

This fix is self-contained and independent — it only touches the tracing-time guard in `is_fake_mode()`.

One heads-up if you reproduce on an sm120 GPU (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50-series): the **end-to-end** FA4 forward path on sm120 also needs the `use_tma_O` fix from #2655. Without #2655, the kernel epilogue raises an unrelated error during the TMA output copy:

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '_trait'
  ... copy_utils.tma_get_copy_fn -> cpasync.tma_partition
```

That crash is **not** caused by this PR (it reproduces in plain eager on sm120 too) — it's the pre-existing TMA-O path that #2655 addresses. With both #2655 and this PR applied, the full check passes on sm120 (torch 2.12, CUDA 13.2):

- `torch.compile(flash_attn_func, fullgraph=True)` traces
- compiled output is bitwise-identical to eager (`max_diff == 0.0`)
- both match SDPA at the bf16 noise floor (`4.9e-4`)

On Hopper (sm90) / sm100 the TMA-O path is unaffected, so this PR stands alone there.

feedback.author: johnnynunez
feedback.body:
### Follow-up: tracing fix is correct, but end-to-end FA4+compile needs more work

To be fully transparent after deeper testing on sm120: this PR makes `flash_attn_func` **traceable** under `torch.compile`, and the standalone check is solid — compiled output is bitwise-identical to eager (`max_diff == 0.0`) on the shapes in the repro.

However, enabling tracing is *not* the same as guaranteeing a correct compiled graph end-to-end. Plugging FA4 into a real model (NVIDIA Cosmos3 DiT) and compiling the whole transformer, I see **shape-dependent NaNs**:

- 256p (seqlen ~4k): compiled latent is finite, output looks sane.
- 480p (seqlen ~16k): the compiled forward produces **NaN** (single-forward `cosine=nan`, `mean|val|=nan`), while the **same FA4 kernel in eager is correct** (`cosine=0.99995` vs native).

So the composition of the CuTeDSL JIT kernel with the inductor graph appears to break on longer sequences — likely a graph-capture / tile-scheduler interaction, not this guard change.

This PR stands on its own merit (the `active_fake_mode` skip was a real, unconditional blocker to *tracing*), but I wanted to flag that **FA4 + torch.compile is not yet numerically safe end-to-end** so nobody ships it expecting correctness on large shapes. Eager FA4 is unaffected and correct. Happy to investigate the NaN path separately if useful.

feedback.author: gemini-code-assist[bot]
feedback.body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The current implementation allows `stem.startswith(lib_name + "-")` to match look-alike stub libraries if they are named with a hyphen instead of an underscore (e.g., `libcudart-stub.so`). Since the hyphen prefix is intended to match packaged hashes (like `libcudart-6479a240.so`), we should explicitly exclude any filenames containing `"stub"` (case-insensitively) to prevent false positives.

```suggestion
            if lib_name not in line or "/" not in line:
                continue
            path = line[line.index("/"):].strip()
            filename = path.split("/")[-1]
            if "stub" in filename.lower():
                continue
            stem = filename.rpartition(".so")[0]
            if stem == lib_name or stem.startswith(lib_name + ".") or stem.startswith(lib_name + "-"):
                return path
```

feedback.author: coderabbitai[bot]
feedback.body:
_🩺 Stability & Availability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Reject dotted look-alike stems.**

`libcudart.foo.so` and `libcudart.sofoo.so` both pass `stem.startswith(lib_name + ".")`. If mapped first, either can still be loaded instead of the real runtime and fail when `CudaRTLibrary` resolves CUDA symbols. A version belongs after `.so`, so it is already handled by `stem == lib_name`.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-            if stem == lib_name or stem.startswith(lib_name + ".") or stem.startswith(lib_name + "-"):
+            if stem == lib_name or (
+                stem.startswith(lib_name + "-") and stem != f"{lib_name}-"
+            ):
                 return path
```
</details>

feedback.author: ormandj
feedback.body:
Reproduced #3676 on SM120 TP2: substring lookup selected TileLang's `libcudart_stub.so`, and FlashInfer workspace initialization failed while binding `cudaDeviceReset`. After replacing substring lookup with filename-based matching, the same `trtllm` configuration initialized its workspace and reached readiness. A later integration run using the resolver carry started with zero restarts and passed semantic correctness. This is initialization evidence, not a performance claim.

I prepared a signed-off commit [`bd6765de`](https://github.com/ormandj/flashinfer/commit/bd6765dea271b23a579938132f8ca1b9cbf6a2a5) directly against this head for both current review findings. Its anchored matcher accepts only `libcudart.so[.N...]` or a nonempty lowercase-hex `libcudart-<hash>.so[.N...]`; it rejects underscore, arbitrary-hyphen, dotted, empty-hash, and path lookalikes. It adds CPU cases for exact, versioned, hash-mangled, collision, load-order, and no-match behavior. This stricter matcher builds on the filename-based resolver approach in #3677 and vllm-project/vllm#47586; credit for those earlier fixes remains with their authors. The focused pytest file passes 12/12 in an isolated uv Python 3.12 environment, and `pre-commit run --all-files` passes every hook. Requesting review of the matcher/test update rather than opening another resolver PR.

feedback.author: ormandj
feedback.body: This fix was adopted in our SM120 stack (SGLang TP2, TileLang installed as an SGLang dependency) after earlier testing hit IPC initialization failures from `find_loaded_library` selecting TileLang's `libcudart_stub.so`. With this PR at `e855cc25` (alongside #3903), TRT-LLM all-reduce workspace initialization succeeds on both ranks and survives CUDA graph capture and replay. Tested on SGLang main `3d91a569ce`, FlashInfer 0.6.14; end-to-end numbers in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3903 and sgl-project/sglang#32330.

feedback.author: ormandj
feedback.body: Correction to the above after discussion with SGLang maintainers: current SGLang main does not need this fix — sgl-project/sglang#30580 (merged Jul 12) lazy-loads TileLang so the stub library is not resident during IPC initialization. Our failure came from a configuration that prewarms TileLang at load. The fix may still be worth having as a robustness improvement in `find_loaded_library` itself, independent of consumer-side workarounds.

feedback.author: vedularaghu
feedback.body:
Worth landing this — the underlying selection bug is still live on `main` and in v0.6.18.
`find_loaded_library` is unchanged, and `CudaRTLibrary.__init__` still calls it with no
`so_file`.

I hit it independently on a serving stack that has TileLang resident before IPC
initialization, so the consumer-side workaround noted above (lazy-loading TileLang) does
not generalize — this really does want fixing in `find_loaded_library` itself, as you
suggested.

Your matcher looks right to me for both spellings a real runtime uses, the plain
`libcudart.so.<ver>` and the hashed `libcudart-<hash>.so.<ver>`, while still rejecting
`libcudart_stub.so`. Worth noting that a simpler-looking tightening to
`filename.startswith(lib_name + ".so")` would silently break the hashed form, so the stem
comparison you went with matters.

One detail that makes this easy to under-prioritize: since 0.6.17 the handle is resolved
lazily, so the original import-time reproduction no longer fails even though the bug is
still there — the failure just moves to the first `cudart.*` access. Details in
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3676#issuecomment-5498963361 rather
than repeating them here. Landing this fixes the selection regardless of when the handle
is resolved.

Is this blocked on anything I can help with? Happy to test a build against a
stub-resident environment if that would move it along.

feedback.author: JinuJeong
feedback.body:
@sufeng-buaa Thanks for pointing this out. Instead of propagating enable_metrics, I separated the two responsibilities:

* `enable_metrics` indicates whether a local metrics collector is available.
* `has_timing_data` indicates that timing data should continue to be propagated across IPC hops.

`__getstate__` now serializes the timing fields when either flag is set and marks the serialized state with has_timing_data=True. This keeps the existing assumption that enable_metrics=True implies a valid collector, while preserving the timing data through the Detokenizer → TokenizerManager hop.

feedback.body:
## Code Review

This pull request removes the fallback to get_openai_tool_schema when initializing BaseTool. The reviewer notes that this change breaks subclasses that dynamically define their schema, and suggests setting self.tool_schema first to avoid potential AttributeError circularity before falling back to get_openai_tool_schema.

feedback.author: gemini-code-assist[bot]
feedback.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Removing the fallback entirely breaks subclasses of `BaseTool` that override `get_openai_tool_schema()` to dynamically define their schema in code (which is a common pattern when `tool_schema` is not provided in the configuration, passing `None` to `__init__`).

To resolve the circular reference/`AttributeError` without breaking subclassing, we can set `self.tool_schema = tool_schema` first. This ensures the attribute exists (even if it is `None`), so calling `self.get_openai_tool_schema()` as a fallback will not raise an `AttributeError` and will correctly invoke the subclass's overridden method.

```suggestion
        self.tool_schema = tool_schema
        if self.tool_schema is None:
            self.tool_schema = self.get_openai_tool_schema()
```

feedback.author: mosya415
feedback.body:
The `ValueError` is real and worth fixing, but I don't think this is the right fix — I'm fairly sure it breaks the incremental path, and the `xfail_streaming` markers in this file hide it.

`extract_intermediate_diff(curr, old)` strips the common prefix and suffix. With `old=""` there's nothing to strip, so it returns `curr` unchanged — this line is just `arguments_delta = cur_arguments_json`.

That's a problem because `partial_json_parser` closes partial JSON for you. Mid-stream, the raw text `{"city": "Dal` re-serializes as `{"city": "Dal"}`, and that trailing `"}` never came from the model. Since streaming only appends, the next delta lands after it:

```
{"city": "Dal"} + las", "state": "TX   ->   {"city": "Dal"}las", "state": "TX
```

Cutting off that synthesized tail is what the `[:index(...) + len(...)]` truncation is for. `extract_intermediate_diff` gets away with it in the `cur_arguments and prev_arguments` branch below because `prev_args_json` has the same closers and they cancel as a common suffix — against `""` there's nothing to cancel.

Repro, no tokenizer needed (realistic token boundaries for `{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Dallas", "state": "TX"}}`):

```python
from vllm.tool_parsers.internlm2_tool_parser import Internlm2ToolParser

DELTAS = [
    "<|action_start|><|plugin|>", '{"', "name", '": "', "get_weather", '", "',
    "parameters", '": {"', "city", '": "', "Dallas", '", "', "state", '": "',
    "TX", '"}}', "<|action_end|>",
]

parser = Internlm2ToolParser(tokenizer=None, tools=[])
streamed, current = "", ""
for delta in DELTAS:
    previous, current = current, current + delta
    msg = parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
        previous_text=previous, current_text=current, delta_text=delta,
        previous_token_ids=[], current_token_ids=[], delta_token_ids=[],
        request=None,
    )
    if msg and msg.tool_calls and msg.tool_calls[0].function:
        streamed += msg.tool_calls[0].function.arguments or ""

print(repr(streamed))
```

main gives `'{"city": "Dallas", "state": "TX'`, a valid prefix that `ensure_json` closes correctly. This PR gives `'{"city": ""}Dallas", "state": "TX'`.

CI won't catch it: the streaming cases here are marked `xfail_streaming`, so the suite reports `9 passed, 16 xfailed` either way.

What I think works — keep the truncation, and only send the value whole once it's actually complete:

```python
match_start = cur_arguments_json.find(delta_text)
if match_start != -1:
    arguments_delta = cur_arguments_json[: match_start + len(delta_text)]
elif is_complete_json(parsable_arr):
    # arguments completed within this delta, so nothing will re-trigger
    # this branch: send them whole rather than dropping them
    arguments_delta = cur_arguments_json
else:
    # still partial and not locatable: wait for more text rather than
    # streaming the closing characters partial_json_parser appended
    return None
```

The `else: return None` keeps the current behaviour of not advancing `prev_tool_call_arr`, so a later delta retries the branch — that retry is why compact-JSON models work on main today.

I ran this: your single-delta case is fixed, the token stream above comes out byte-identical to main, and the suite still reports `9 passed, 16 xfailed`. Same bug exists in `jamba_tool_parser.py` on the same lines; I'm fixing it there the same way.

feedback.author: chuenchen309
feedback.body:
You're completely right, and thank you for the thorough analysis and the tokenizer-free repro — that makes the failure obvious. My change drops the `[:index(delta_text) + len(delta_text)]` truncation, but that truncation is load-bearing: `partial_json_parser` closes the partial object, so mid-stream `{"city": "Dal` re-serializes to `{"city": "Dal"}` and the synthesized `"}` has to be cut before the next append, otherwise it lands inline as `{"city": "Dal"}las", ...`. The `cur_arguments and prev_arguments` branch only gets away without it because `prev_args_json` carries the same closers and they cancel as a common suffix — against `old=""` there's nothing to cancel, exactly as you said. And yes, the `xfail_streaming` markers hid the regression from CI.

Your fix is the correct one: keep the truncation, `find(delta_text)`, send whole only when the arguments are actually complete, and otherwise `return None` so a later delta retries the branch (which is what keeps the compact-JSON path working today).

Since you've already implemented and byte-verified this, and you're fixing the identical bug in `jamba_tool_parser.py` the same way, it's cleanest for both files to go together in your PR — please go ahead and include internlm2 there, and I'll close this one in favor of it. Happy to review/test if that helps. Thanks again for catching that my patch traded one bug for a subtler one.
